title: Copper-, nickel- and zinc-based trimetallic (CuNiZn–BDC) MOFs as efficient adsorbents for the adsorptive removal of metanil yellow from wastewater
content: Herein, a trimetallic metal–organic framework was synthesized (abbreviated as TM-CuNiZn–BDC MOF) via a solvothermal method. The TM-CuNiZn–BDC MOF was comprehensively characterized by EDX, SEM, elemental mapping, XRD, FTIR spectroscopy, BET, zeta potential analysis, and TGA. FTIR spectroscopy confirmed the presence of key functional groups, while XRD revealed crystallinity with clear, sharp, and distinct diffraction peaks. TGA indicated stability up to 600 °C. The estimated surface area from BET analysis was 654 m2 g−1. The synthesized MOF exhibited a nanoscale size of approximately 98.3 nm with agglomerates of around 259 nm. Under optimal experimental conditions, such as 0.01 g adsorbent dosage, pH 6, 60 °C and 60 min contact time, the MOF achieved >93% removal efficiency for metanil yellow dye. Kinetic investigations revealed that the process followed second-order kinetics, as evidenced by the linear correlation (R2 = 0.99), while the adsorption capacity recorded was 689 mg g−1 at 333 K. The adsorption was spontaneous with a negative ΔG° value and endothermic with a positive ΔH°; the adsorption mechanism was governed by chemisorption, hydrogen bonding, electrostatic attraction, π–π interactions and pore filling. The TM-CuNiZn–BDC MOF retained its structural stability and 54% removal efficiency after seven reuse cycles, demonstrating its strong potential as a robust and efficient wastewater adsorbent.
